values.note: 22 sites 'suitable for tent camping and medium sized RV's'; BLM's site map gives each spur's length: most 28-52 ft (site 1 is 52, 12 is 50), a few short ones (6 at 23 ft, 19 at about 21 ft). Two vehicles and eight people per site. recreation.gov also lists a tent loop (23-31) as not available.

sites.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co ('Mill Creek Campground has 22 campsites suitable for tent camping and medium sized RV's. Each campsite is limited to eight people and two vehicles') + BLM site map PDF (site 1 '52'', 12 '50'', 10 '45'', 6 '23'') + recreation.gov catalog 271727 (sites A 1-22, Max Vehicle Length 18-50; Tent Loop 23-31 'Not Available'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: Hand pumps; bear-proof food box at every site and bear-proof dumpsters at the entrance (no trash pickup at sites). Hosts June to early September.

facilities.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co ('Mill Creek Campground has vault restrooms, hand pumps for potable water, and bear-proof trash dumpsters on site'; 'Campground hosts are available from June through early September') + BLM site map ('Campsites do not have individual trash pickup. Please put trash in dumpsters at entrance'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: BLM: 'The campground is accessible June through September.' Reservations run Memorial Day to Sept 30.

season.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co ('The campground is accessible June through September'; 'RESERVABLE up to 180-days in advance during peak season, Memorial Day through September 30th'), read 2026-10-28

values.note: 13 sites reservable on recreation.gov up to 180 days ahead in the peak season (Memorial Day - Sept 30); the other 9 first-come, paid on site with the recreation.gov app, cash or check. No changes within 72 hours of arrival. Camping limited to 2 weeks. 2027 reservation season May 27 - Sept 30.

booking.source: https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co ('At Mill Creek Campground thirteen sites are RESERVABLE up to 180-days in advance during peak season, Memorial Day through September 30th. The remaining nine sites are FIRST COME, FIRST SERVED with camp fee paid on site with Recreation.gov app (preferred), cash or check'; 'Reservations cannot be modified less than 72 hours prior') + BLM site map ('Camping is limited to 2 weeks') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/271727/rates (Peak Season 2027-05-27 to 2027-09-30), read 2026-10-28

note: BLM (Gunnison Field Office), 14 mi SW of Lake City at 9,500 ft, across a bridge from Cinnamon Pass Rd (CR 30) on the Lake Fork of the Gunnison. Shaded sites in spruce-fir and aspen; a fishing access trail leads to the river. Base camp for the Alpine Loop Backcountry Byway, which is for licensed OHVs and high-clearance 4WD beyond the campground. --Claude
summary: BLM page + BLM site map + rec.gov: confirmed 22 sites, max 52 ft (BLM map, site 1), no hookups, $20, 13 reservable + 9 FCFS; added vault toilets, hand-pump water, season (BLM 'June through September', no dates), 180-day window, 14-night limit, booking.season 05-27 to 09-30. Note rewritten without field facts.
flags: Phone: (970) 642-4953 is the campground's BLM contact (BLM page 'Contact Us kacarson@blm.gov (970) 642-4953'; also recreation.gov's facility phone). The Gunnison Field Office main line is 970-642-4940 (https://www.blm.gov/office/gunnison-field-office; also the BLM page's 'For facility specific information, please call (970) 642-4940'). Either is official; the office line may be the better listed number.
Website: recreation.gov only; add the BLM page https://www.blm.gov/visit/mill-creek-campground-co.

Max length: 52 ft is a BLM figure (site 1 on BLM's 'Campground Map with site dimensions'), not only the catalog (catalog max 50). RIG-LENGTH WORDING: BLM says '22 campsites suitable for tent camping and medium sized RV's' - general wording, outranked by the same agency's per-site dimensions (most 28-52 ft).

Access: recreation.gov notice 'Maintained gravel road to campground, beyond campground 4X4 recommended'; directions CO-149 south 2 mi, CR 30 10.5 mi, 'on the left, over the bridge'. The 4x4 recommendation is for the Alpine Loop beyond the campground, not the route to it.

Waterfront (stored not waterfront) - re-audit lead: BLM says the campground is 'Nestled along the Lake Fork of the Gunnison River' with a fishing access trail. On imagery with catalog points the Lake Fork (~10-15 m wide, creek-sized) runs along the north side of the loop; the nearest sites (16, 13, 12) are ~30-60 m from it through dense spruce, no open apron. Creekside might be arguable for site 16; canopy hides it. Not changed.

Count: BLM 22 (13 reservable + 9 first-come); recreation.gov catalog has 22 A-loop sites (14 marked reservable) plus a Tent Loop 23-31 marked 'Not Available' (possibly the expansion BLM solicited in 2025).
Pin 37.90726,-107.39283 (= BLM/recreation.gov coordinate) is at the CR 30 bridge entrance, ~220 m WSW of the catalog site centroid 37.90650,-107.39052. Under 500 m.
Status: no closure posted; the reservation season ended Sept 30.
